correspondence.component_scope: High-volcano opening and Excola–Calcahualco valley
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the northeastern Pico de Orizaba flank and follows the mapped stream northeast toward Excola, then east through the Calcahualco setting. The continuous blue stream is visible across the initial slope and connecting valley. The nearby west-draining stream and the separate east/southeast course toward Coscomatepec are not substituted for this opening. A modern glacier-source or current perennial-flow claim is not made.

correspondence.component_scope: Tozongo–Ixhuatlán del Café–Tlamatoca bend
correspondence.finding: The source follows the selected southeast descent by Tozongo and the southern bend near Ixhuatlán del Café, then the northward return toward Tlamatoca. The distinct southern drainage toward Chocamán is outside the selected route. Both bends and their intervening through-link are established by the original.

correspondence.component_scope: Tepatlaxco–La Palma and named Jamapa central bend
correspondence.finding: The mapped stream turns southeast past Tepatlaxco and La Palma, continues east around the broad southern bend, and turns northeast into the plain. Río Jamapa is directly printed along this selected river, rather than inferred from a town or basin name.

correspondence.component_scope: Camarón de Tejeda–Soledad de Doblado–La Matamba plain
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward meandering corridor is continuous through the Camarón de Tejeda and Soledad de Doblado setting toward La Matamba. The separately labeled Río Chiquito approaches from the north and joins the Jamapa corridor; its upstream course is not a selected fragment. No lake, reservoir or canal transfer is shown interrupting the selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Jamapa town to Medellín and lower confluence approach
correspondence.finding: The western river winds past the Jamapa settlement, turns southeast, and continues east into the Medellín setting. Its last selected part approaches the lower junction from the west. The substantial separate southern river through Paso del Toro is mapped entering this lower corridor; its unselected upstream reach is not assigned the Jamapa scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower confluence, estuarine turn and Gulf terminal
correspondence.finding: The second mainstem fragment continues the same lower river through the confluence setting, turns north and then east/northeast to the direct Gulf opening at Boca del Río. All four parts are accounted for. The Mandinga Grande lagoon and its coastal connecting channel lie east/southeast of the selected river; the selection does not pass through that lagoon. The final coastal crossing is supported at ordinary generalized scale, without an exact shoreline or mouth-vertex claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and northward inland-ice sequence
correspondence.finding: The entire chosen opening and its successive northward parts lie within the regional original’s mapped inland-ice area. The source covers the opening and intervening joins continuously. Its ice and topographic contours do not establish a named surface river or a subglacial watercourse.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern turn toward the eastern Tasersiaq setting
correspondence.finding: The westward northern turn and subsequent southwestward steps occupy the historical mapped inland-ice/exposed-rock margin adjoining the eastern Tasersiaq setting. The original distinguishes ice, colored rock units and neighboring white waterbody outlines. This geographic correspondence does not establish an inflow, outlet or river continuation through that waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Long westward ice-and-rock corridor along the southern Tasersiaq setting
correspondence.finding: All westward parts and intermediate joins are visible along the mixed exposed-rock and ice-margin belt at and south of the mapped Tasersiaq waterbody. The selected line is not demonstrated to be wholly within the lake or a continuous mapped river channel. Tasersiaq is a neighboring waterbody label; it is not applied as a name for this modeled river group.

correspondence.component_scope: Western bend and transition into the southwestward corridor
correspondence.finding: The local northward and westward bend at the western Tasersiaq setting is covered in the same original. The selected succession enters an elongated exposed-rock/ice-margin corridor southwest of that waterbody. The mapping does not establish a hydraulic lake-outlet-to-river through-link along the selected sequence.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward approach toward inner Evighedsfjord
correspondence.finding: The complete southwestward approach and its short selected parts follow the generalized exposed-rock and ice-margin corridor toward the northeastern inner branch of the mapped Evighedsfjord coastal-water setting. Adjacent ice, bedrock ridges and the inlet are distinguishable. No named glacier or natural-river reach is assigned, and terrain correspondence is not hydraulic continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final part and selected terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The entire final selected part and actual ending are covered at the historical mapped ice/exposed-rock margin adjoining the inner Evighedsfjord coastal-water setting. The original distinguishes the surrounding ice, rock and white inlet. The model’s sea-terminal classification is not independent evidence of an ordinary river mouth. The map does not establish exact present-day ice-front position or a precise modern ice/land/water assignment at the endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and Rosemary Creek pond/channel corridor
correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening lies on the mapped Rosemary Creek corridor southwest of Williston, near the Rosemary Street crossing. The connected creek continues south through the Tanglewood Road surroundings, receives the distinct eastern channel from Folk Pond, and passes through small unnamed on-channel waterbodies near Lin Road and the US278 crossing. Original cartography shows the river entering and leaving these waterbodies and continuing into the southern wetland corridor. Sister Lake and Folk Pond are not the selected opening or substituted names for this creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Rosemary–Buck joining setting and upper Salkehatchie River
correspondence.finding: South of Pioneer Road the selected Rosemary Creek bends southeast and meets the mapped Buck Creek corridor near Seven Bridges Road. The connecting downstream channel is labelled Salkehatchie River. The selected line follows this named trunk south along the wooded wetland corridor west of Barnwell and through the SC64 crossing. Buck Creek and Bolen Pond lie on the separate eastern contributing branch; no whole upstream branch is relabelled Combahee.

correspondence.component_scope: Barnwell bend and Turkey, Toby and Hurricane Creek junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected Salkehatchie River curves southeast past the southern side of Barnwell and the Turkey Creek junction, crosses the US278 setting, then continues east into the Toby Creek and Hurricane Creek joining area. The connected source channel and repeated Salkehatchie labels support the actual river corridor. Edgar A Brown Lake belongs to the separate Turkey Creek approach and Fuller Pond lies on a separate southern tributary; neither is traversed by the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Olar–Schofield corridor and Bufords Bridge
correspondence.finding: Below the Toby and Hurricane Creek setting the Salkehatchie continues east through the Hercules Creek and George Creek junctions, then turns southeast through the Birds Branch and Schofield surroundings. The map follows the connected river past Wells Branch to the Bufords Bridge/US301 crossing, northeast of Ulmer. The selected simplification remains in this connected floodplain-channel corridor rather than transferring to a nearby isolated pond.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Salkehatchie to Broxton Bridge
correspondence.finding: The connected river continues southeast from Bufords Bridge through the Kirkland Creek and Bear Branch joins, the Rivers Bridge Road and Threemile Branch settings, and the SC641 crossing. Farther downstream it passes the Calico Branch/Jenny Pond tributary setting and the Broxton Bridge/US601 crossing. Repeated Salkehatchie River labels and connected hydrographic linework cover the selected passage through the extensive forested wetland. Jenny Pond and the elongated Threemile Branch waterbody remain on distinct contributing channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Moselle, Tobys Bluff and Whippy Swamp passage
correspondence.finding: Below Broxton Bridge the named Salkehatchie runs southeast beside Moselle and Miley through the broad multi-channel wetland. It passes the Moselle Swamp surroundings, reaches Tobys Bluff, and receives the Whippy Swamp channel at the SC63 crossing. The source continues the selected river southeast through the wetland toward the Little Salkehatchie approach. The mapped connected channels provide the ordinary through-corridor; exact braid or seasonal channel choice is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Salkehatchie–Little Salkehatchie confluence and Combahee transition
correspondence.finding: The cartography distinguishes the selected Salkehatchie corridor on the west from the incoming Little Salkehatchie River on the east. Their connected branches meet in the Horse Bay, Sandy Run, Tennants Branch and Bull Creek joining setting. Below the joining area the receiving channel is explicitly labelled Combahee River. The selected route follows the incoming Salkehatchie and the downstream Combahee, not the upper Little Salkehatchie branch. This is a mapped confluence and receiving-river transition, without a formal name-boundary vertex claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Combahee, Black Creek and the Yemassee-area crossings
correspondence.finding: The named Combahee continues south past the Black Creek confluence, crosses Interstate95 and the road/rail setting at Salkehatchie east of Yemassee, and bends southeast toward Blake. The connected source channel covers all selected joins between the wooded wetland reach and the increasingly broad tidal meanders. Big Survey Lake is on the separate Black Creek branch and is not a selected lake transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Blake and lower Combahee tidal bends through US17
correspondence.finding: The selected river follows the connected Combahee meanders east from Blake along the Beaufort–Colleton boundary, through the refuge and managed-marsh surroundings, and past the White Hall tributary joining setting. It turns south through the US17 crossing and continues through the broad lower tidal bends. Nearby rectangular wetland/impoundment features are not substituted as the selected through-route; current water-control states are not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower meanders, Tar Bluff and Gunboat Island
correspondence.finding: Below US17 the selected route follows the large mapped Combahee water channel southeast, then around Tar Bluff, Old Combahee Island and Gunboat Island. The river remains continuous through these substantial bends and the Fields Point setting. Williman Creek and the Chehaw river network are separately depicted adjoining tidal waters, not replacement names for the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal in the lower Combahee tidal reach
correspondence.finding: The final selected segment leaves the last large bend near Fields Point and ends at the western side of the broad Combahee River beside the Chehaw joining setting. A focused original crop and separate private orientation aid confirm the actual endpoint, rather than substituting a presumed ocean mouth. The source labels the broad reach Combahee River and depicts it continuing south to Coosaw River. The short model tail and locally clipped meanders are ordinary cartographic generalizations; precise present bank position and current tide are not established.
